chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The one who has food to give, it is not for him to fast; he should feed ten poor people, a handful, a handful. And the one who cannot find [food], he should fast for three days.

key_terms.مُدّاً مُدّاً: A handful, a handful (measure of food)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a hierarchical structure for expiating broken oaths, prioritizing feeding ten poor people (one mud each) over fasting three days for those unable to afford the former. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (taysir), ensuring that financial incapacity does not become a barrier to fulfilling religious obligations, while maintaining the spiritual discipline of fasting as a secondary remedy.
